"hi, everyone. last month we got news one of our cats at lot 50, nefarious (aka double cheeseburger) had a neck injury that we have been keeping a close eye on. over the past two weeks it has progressed at a rapid rate, and we were able to set up an emergency group of members to begin attempts at trapping him on monday. this morning miranda and lynn were able to trap him and bring him to cityvet, where their team sedated him and determined humane euthanasia was the best course in order to prevent further suffering.

from miranda: "he was a patriarch of the colony, an old soul that the other cats all respected. while he wasn't fond of people all too much, he enjoyed staring at us. he kept the colony in line when cats got too erratic and would put tomcats in their place.
in the end, he died as he lived. a fighter. he was smart, too smart for his own good. he stuck through it just because he didn't want us to help him. he made us crawl through a large patch of thorns just to get him. through his pain, i think he enjoyed our struggle. he will always be keeping lot 50 in line.""

author: slayc127
content:
i want us to not just ignore when we have members bring an injured cat to our attention. we cant save every cat, but we also have members that respect us and for us to ignore them and not give a specific reason why we cant trap a cat that is showing obvious signs of injury and rapid progression will only make them feel as if we do not care or do not prioritize cats. if we make the decision we are not going to bring a cat in, we need to be able to back that up and justify it. if we make the decision to wait and see if the wound/injury gets worse, we need to be able to state that plainly. that didnt happen here because we just didnt address it. 
i understand we are always going to be worried about money and about our availability as officers, and that the second part will be addressed as we get more officers coming in, but i feel like it is such a disservice to not take advantage of how much support we have currently that was shown to us with so many members showing up to help with tnr. we are here for the cats, first and foremost, and this situation doesnt necessarily help support that. im trying to not be too confrontational or self righteous because it isnt my intention, im just not sure how else to frame it at the moment

Historically, wounds that present as cat bites/scrapes we've just kept an eye on until they've progressed and then planned course of action. For nef, we did typical course of action and when it progressed we did what we could. Are we wanting to change that? As in when we see a wound do we immediately send the cat to the vet or do we continue to sit and watch? This situation is bound to repeat and nef's injuries were unexpected as most injuries are in feral cats. Same with the rubber situation, before we all get on edge I'd like to bypass that stage of discussion and just get down to a solution. So i think we need to decide how we go about injuries from now on, sit and wait or vet regardless?
